Durchläuchtigſter Fürſt.
Gnädigster Herr!
Ew Hochfürstlichen Durchlaucht denke ich
unterthänigst, für die Aufschluße, die
Höchstdieselben in der Güther-Vertauschungs¬
Angelegenheit nur zu ertheilen geruhet
haben. Dabey ist es mir eine unendliche
Freude, daß Sr. Majestät die angetragenen
weitere Untersuchung verfügt haben,
und versicher ich unterthänigst, daß ich im
weitern Verfolg dieser Angelegenheit
meine Pflichten eben so gewißenhaft als
bisher beobachten, also auch keinen Auswegen
unversucht laßen werde, der die Wünsche
Ew Hochfürstlichen Durchlaucht, die Geneigt
heit meines Herrn ihnen entgegen zu
kommen und des Interesse des Staats mit
ein

einander zu vereinigen im Stande
seyn wird. Dieser Versicherung füge
ich die Betheuerung der unbegrenz¬
testen Ehrerbietigkeit hinzu, womit
ich lebenslang verharre
Ew Hochfürstlichen Durchlaucht
unterthänigster Diener
Beyme
Berlin
den 17ten Xbr.
1798.

translation.en: Most Serene Prince. Most gracious Lord! To Your Most Serene Highness I render most humble thanks for the elucidations which You have been pleased only to impart in the matter of the exchange of estates. It is withal an infinite joy to me that His Majesty has ordered the further investigation which was proposed, and I most humbly give assurance that in the further pursuit of this matter I shall observe my duties just as conscientiously as hitherto, and shall therefore also leave no expedient [uncertain: unattempted] which shall be capable of reconciling with one another the wishes of Your Most Serene Highness, the inclination of my Lord to meet them, and the interest of the State.

...will be able to reconcile with one another. To this assurance I add the protestation of the most unbounded reverence, wherewith I remain lifelong Your Most Serene Highness's most humble and obedient servant Beyme Berlin, the 17th of December 1798.

text_english:
Most Serene Prince. Most gracious Lord! To Your Most Serene Highness I render most humble thanks for the elucidations which You have been pleased only to impart in the matter of the exchange of estates. It is withal an infinite joy to me that His Majesty has ordered the further investigation which was proposed, and I most humbly give assurance that in the further pursuit of this matter I shall observe my duties just as conscientiously as hitherto, and shall therefore also leave no expedient [uncertain: unattempted] which shall be capable of reconciling with one another the wishes of Your Most Serene Highness, the inclination of my Lord to meet them, and the interest of the State.

...will be able to reconcile with one another. To this assurance I add the protestation of the most unbounded reverence, wherewith I remain lifelong Your Most Serene Highness's most humble and obedient servant Beyme Berlin, the 17th of December 1798.
summary_en: Beyme, writing from Berlin, thanks the Prince for the explanations given concerning the proposed exchange of estates, and expresses satisfaction that His Majesty has ordered the further investigation that had been suggested. He pledges to pursue the business as conscientiously as before and to leave no expedient untried that might reconcile the Prince's wishes, the King's willingness to accommodate them, and the interest of the State, closing with assurances of reverence.
summary_de: Dank für die vom Fürsten erteilten Aufklärungen in der Sache des Gütertausches; Beyme äußert seine Freude darüber, daß Seine Majestät die vorgeschlagene weitere Untersuchung angeordnet hat, und versichert, die Angelegenheit ebenso gewissenhaft wie bisher weiterzuverfolgen und kein Mittel unversucht zu lassen, um die Wünsche des Fürsten, die Bereitwilligkeit seines Herrn und das Interesse des Staates miteinander zu vereinigen. Schluß mit Ergebenheitsbekundungen; sachliche Angaben zu Gütern oder Summen fehlen.
